---
title: "0002 Separate core and binding crates"
date: 2026-10-18
status: accepted
basis: evidence
---

## Decision

The Rust code is a cargo workspace with two crates:

- `crates/ume-core`: pure Rust kernels with no Python dependency.
- `crates/ume-python`: PyO3 bindings only, compiled into `ume._core`.

## Alternatives

One crate that holds both the kernels and the `#[pyfunction]` wrappers. This is maturin's default template.

## Justification

- With PyO3's `extension-module` feature, the crate does not link against libpython, so `cargo test` binaries for that crate fail to link. This is a documented PyO3 limitation. Kernels in a separate crate can be unit tested, doc tested and benchmarked with plain `cargo`.
- The binding layer stays thin and easy to audit: convert arrays, release the GIL, call the core, map errors.
- The core can be reused by other bindings without pulling in Python (see [0001](0001-python-api-rust-core.qmd)).

Cost: one extra `Cargo.toml`. The workspace shares version, edition and lints, so the crates cannot drift apart.
